# InputContext

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("InputContext")`

A group of `InputAction` children that are live together (§2.4, ADR 0029). A menu opening is one context enabled and another disabled, rather than a pile of conditionals inside every handler. Parent it anywhere -- the convention is under the Script that owns it -- because a context is reached by being enabled, not by where it sits.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this context and its actions take part in resolution at all. A disabled context consumes nothing, so a lower-priority one bound to the same key starts firing the tick this goes false -- which is exactly what closing a menu should do. |
| `Priority` | `number` | `0` | read/write | Resolution order, highest first. It orders FALLTHROUGH and nothing else -- in particular it does not decide which clock the context is dispatched on, which is `Rate` (ADR 0039). Ties are broken by a stable order the engine reproduces on every run (R10), so two contexts at the same priority never swap places between one run and the next. |
| `Rate` | `Enum.InputRate` | `Enum.InputRate.Simulation` | read/write | Which clock this context is dispatched on (ADR 0039). `Simulation` by default, because that is the safe one: an action nobody thought about fires where R10 holds and where the input replay can see it. `Render` is for camera look and for UI, and an action read from a Render context is frame-rate-dependent by construction. |
| `Sink` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether this context CONSUMES the inputs its bindings name, hiding them from every lower-priority context. A modal dialog sinks; a HUD does not. Sinking is per input and not per context: a sinking context that binds Escape hides Escape and leaves W alone. |
